summary: build.rs exfiltrates full environment to base64-hidden webhook.site endpoint with scanner-evasion gating
details: The crate's build.rs snapshots the complete process environment via env::vars() with no name filtering, augments it with HOSTNAME/USER, serializes it to JSON (up to 8 KiB per value), writes it to OUT_DIR, and POSTs it to a base64-encoded webhook.site URL (https://webhook.site/14b3cc9b-3275-4b63-8b93-f4d2669fbdc1) using a detached `/bin/sh -c 'curl -s -X POST... &'` on Unix and a hidden PowerShell `iwr` on Windows. The destination string is reconstructed at runtime by an inlined base64 decoder (b64d) rather than appearing in cleartext. Before sending, a `noisy` gate checks environment values against a base64-encoded keyword list including `canary`, `phylum`, `socket.dev`, `sandbox`, `honeypot`, and `example.com`, and silently skips the upload when any match — suppressing the beacon inside common security-analysis environments while firing on developer workstations and CI runners. The build script runs on every `cargo build`/`check`/`test`, including IDE-triggered invocations, so unfiltered environments routinely contain CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, NPM_TOKEN, and similar secrets. The advertised crate purpose (canonicalizing Zcash lightwalletd URIs) has no legitimate need for build-time environment capture, and comments framing the behavior as 'reproducible-build context snapshot' / 'provenance debugging' are inconsistent with the obfuscation and sandbox-evasion logic.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
